rules.sentence: In 1967, a similarly structured valve, the Starr-Edwards cage-and-ball valve, was implanted 1000 times for mitral valve disease.[9]
The first artificial valve, the Hufnagel cage-and-ball valve, was introduced in 1952 and was placed in the descending thoracic aorta to prevent blood flow reversal in aortic regurgitation.

In 1944, cardiac surgeons Blalock, Taussig, and Thomas made their first venture into the field of congenital heart lesions by operating on a patient with tetralogy of Fallot—a cyanotic heart defect.[10]
Pulmonary stenosis is another cyanotic heart lesion.[11]
For cardiac arrhythmias, the Cox-Maze procedure provides a surgical treatment for atrial fibrillation.
To treat proximal aortic dissection or aneurysm, Bentall developed a procedure that combines the implantation of an artificial aortic valve with an ascending aortic vessel prosthesis.
